The '''Bulls–Cavaliers rivalry''' is a [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) [[List of National Basketball Association rivalries|rivalry]] between the [[Chicago Bulls]] and the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].  The teams have played each other since the Cavaliers joined the NBA as an [[expansion team]] in 1970, but the rivalry did not begin in earnest until the Bulls drafted [[Michael Jordan]] with the third overall pick in [[1984 NBA Draft|1984]]. After Jordan would go on to the [[Washington Wizards]] and eventually retire, the rivalry died down, but when Cleveland picked [[LeBron James]] with the first selection in [[2003 NBA Draft|2003]], the rivalry heated up again.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Swartz |first1=Greg |title=Memorable Bulls-Cavaliers Rivalry Picks Up Right Where It Left Off |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2179948-memorable-bulls-cavaliers-rivalry-picks-up-right-where-it-left-off |website=Bleacher Report |publisher=Turner |access-date=26 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140901034443/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2179948-memorable-bulls-cavaliers-rivalry-picks-up-right-where-it-left-off |archive-date=September 1, 2014 |date=August 29, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Johnson |first1=K. C. |title=Derrick Rose and Kyrie Irving ready for Bulls-Cavs rivalry |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/2014/09/12/derrick-rose-and-kyrie-irving-ready-for-bulls-cavs-rivalry/ |website=Chicago Tribune |publisher=Tribune Publishing |access-date=26 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250623025852/https://www.chicagotribune.com/2014/09/12/derrick-rose-and-kyrie-irving-ready-for-bulls-cavs-rivalry/ |archive-date=June 23, 2025 |date=September 12, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Krishnamurthy |first1=Aaditya |title=Joakim Noah On LeBron James Mocking The Bulls During Their Rivalry: "He Was Arrogant" |website=The Robesonian |publisher=Associated Press |date=April 26, 1994 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Cavs fend off Bulls to end streak In 2011, Bleacher Report named the Bulls as the Cavaliers' "Greatest Rivalry."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Favale |first1=Dan |title=NBA: Each Team's Greatest Rivalry |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/794973-greatest-rivalry-from-every-nba-team |website=Bleacher Report |access-date=26 August 2025 |date=August 8, 2011}}</ref> The NBA called it "one of the great NBA rivalries."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Smith |first1=Sam |title=Greatest Moments in Bulls vs. Cavaliers History |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/features/samsmith/greatest-moments-bulls-vs-cavaliers-history |website=NBA |access-date=26 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161202113332/https://www.nba.com/bulls/features/samsmith/greatest-moments-bulls-vs-cavaliers-history |archive-date=December 2, 2016 |date=November 29, 2016}}</ref>

==The Michael Jordan era==
Chicago had the third selection in the [[1984 NBA draft]], and selected [[Michael Jordan]] out of [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]]. Jordan won the [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award]] in 1985 and led the Bulls to a {{win-loss record|w=38|l=44}} record and the seventh seed in the Eastern Conference. As for Cleveland, they had a {{win-loss record|w=36|l=46}} record, just a single seed under Chicago with the eighth seed. The Cavaliers wouldn't play the Bulls in the [[NBA playoffs|playoffs]] until [[1988 NBA playoffs|1988]], which the Bulls would win, {{win-loss record|w=3|l=2}}.

===The Shot===

Back when the first round was [[NBA playoffs|best-of-5]] instead of [[NBA playoffs|best-of-7]], it was game 5 of the [[1989 NBA playoffs|First Round in 1989]], on May 7, Jordan hit what is known today as "[[The Shot (Bulls–Cavaliers)|The Shot]]" even with Cleveland sweeping Chicago in the season, it wasn't enough to get by Jordan's shot to win and play the [[1988–89 New York Knicks season|Knicks]] the next round. [[Craig Ehlo]] was the player Jordan shot over to win the game. The Cavaliers wouldn't play the Bulls in the playoffs until the [[1992 NBA playoffs|1992 Eastern Conference Finals]], which Chicago would win yet again {{win-loss record|w=4|l=2}}. The Shot is remembered by Cleveland fans as part of the [[Cleveland sports curse]], along with [[The Drive (American football)|The Drive]], [[The Fumble]] and [[Red Right 88]].

A sequel to "The Shot" occurred at the end of Game 4 of the [[1993 NBA playoffs|1993 Eastern Conference Semifinals]], again with Jordan hitting a series-winning shot on the same end of the [[Richfield Coliseum]] floor as in 1989. The Bulls swept the Cavaliers en route to their third consecutive title. Then in the [[1994 NBA playoffs|1994 First Round]], the Bulls again swept the Cavaliers despite Jordan retiring for the first time the previous autumn.

A notable regular season moment between the two teams took place on March 28, 1990, at the Richfield Coliseum. In the Bulls' 117–113 overtime win over the Cavaliers, Jordan scored a career-high 69 points along with 18 rebounds, six assists and four steals, while playing all but three minutes in the game.

The Bulls would win six [[List of NBA champions|NBA championships]] with Jordan and his partner [[Scottie Pippen]],  and 3 of those championships with [[Dennis Rodman]].

==The LeBron James era==
The Cleveland Cavaliers were dominated by the Bulls in the rivalry, even with likes of [[Mark Price]], [[Steve Kerr]], [[Ron Harper]] and others playing the franchise, Jordan was too much to handle and adding [[Scottie Pippen]] made it even more difficult on the Cavaliers, but Jordan would eventually retire and Pippen was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]]. Cleveland would have the first pick in the [[2003 NBA draft]]<ref>{{cite web|title=NBA Draft history: 2003 Draft|url=http://www.nba.com/history/draft/2003-draft/|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=February 27, 2013|access-date=June 5, 2017}}</ref> and used that selection to pick [[LeBron James]]. The Cavaliers would take over the rivalry with LeBron, Chicago would pick a hometown player with the first pick as well in [[Derrick Rose]].<ref>{{cite web|title=NBA Draft history: 2008 Draft|url=http://www.nba.com/history/draft/2008-draft/|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=February 27, 2013|access-date=June 5, 2017}}</ref> However, Rose had an injury in the playoffs against Philadelphia that would deter Rose's promising career that won him the MVP in [[2010–11 NBA season|2011]]. Both teams met up in the first round in 2010, and Cleveland won their first ever series against Chicago, {{win-loss record|w=4|l=1}}. They would play again in 2015 which Cleveland won again, {{win-loss record|w=4|l=2}}.

===Bulls' resurgence===
[[File:Kyrie_Irving_(32963168585).jpg|right|thumb|180px|The Cavaliers drafted Irving [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall]] in 2011.]]
In the summer of 2010, Cavaliers superstar LeBron James became a free agent, and announced on [[ESPN]] that he would [[The Decision (TV special)|join]] the [[Miami Heat]], to join [[Chris Bosh]] and [[Dwyane Wade]]. [[2010–11 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland's first season]] without James was an awful year, finishing with a record of {{Win–loss record|w=19|l=63}}. Meanwhile, the [[2010–11 Chicago Bulls season|Bulls]] finished {{Win–loss record|w=62|l=20}} and earned the first seed in the [[2011 NBA playoffs|Eastern Conference playoffs]]; Derrick Rose would win the [[NBA Most Valuable Player Award|NBA MVP]]. However, the Bulls lost in the [[NBA Conference Finals|Eastern Conference finals]] against the [[2010–11 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]], who would lose in the [[2011 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] against the [[2010–11 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]]. Cleveland would draft [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] point guard [[Kyrie Irving]] with the first pick and [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] center [[Tristan Thompson]] with the fourth pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=NBA Draft history: 2011 Draft|url=http://www.nba.com/history/draft/2011-draft/|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=February 27, 2013|access-date=June 5, 2017}}</ref> Irving would win the Rookie of the Year Award. However, the Cavaliers' best season without James was when they finished {{Win–loss record|w=33|l=49}} in [[2013–14 Cleveland Cavaliers season|2013–14]].

=== Return of LeBron James, 2015 semifinals rematch ===
On July 11, 2014, James announced his return to Cleveland in a letter published to ''[[Sports Illustrated]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2014/07/11/lebron-james-cleveland-cavaliers|title=LeBron: I'm coming back to Cleveland|author1=LeBron James|author2=Lee Jenkins|date=July 11, 2014|access-date=June 5, 2017|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref> The Cavaliers would select [[Andrew Wiggins]] in [[2014 NBA Draft|2014]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://stats.nba.com/draft/history/#!?Season=2014|title=NBA.com/Stats–2014 Draft History|publisher=National Basketball Association|access-date=June 5, 2017}}</ref> first overall, who they would trade along with [[Anthony Bennett (basketball)|Anthony Bennett]] to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in exchange for [[Kevin Love]]. Both the Bulls and Cavaliers would qualify to play in the [[2015 NBA playoffs|playoffs]].

The [[2014–15 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cavaliers]] earned the Eastern Conference's second seed, and the [[2014–15 Chicago Bulls season|Bulls]] earned the third seed. The teams would play each other in the Eastern Conference semi-finals. Chicago won game 1 with Derrick Rose scoring 25 points. Cleveland won game 2 with James scoring 33 points. Chicago won game 3, as Derrick Rose made a shot as time expired. Cleveland won game 4, as James also made a shot as time expired. The Cavaliers would also win games 5 and 6 to eliminate the Bulls, and advanced to play in the [[2015 NBA Finals]], where they would lose to the [[2014–15 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]] in 6 games. The Cavaliers played Golden State in the [[NBA Finals]] again the [[2016 NBA Finals|next year]] and came back from a {{win-loss record|w=3|l=1}} series deficit to end the [[Cleveland sports curse|52-year championship drought]] in Cleveland.

== LeBron leaves again, both teams start rebuilds ==
During the [[2017 NBA draft]] the Bulls traded all-star [[Jimmy Butler]] to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in exchange for the 7th overall pick (used to pick [[Lauri Markkanen]]), [[Zach LaVine]] and [[Kris Dunn]] to start a rebuild for the Bulls. Meanwhile, for Cleveland they traded superstar [[Kyrie Irving]] (upon request) to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for [[Isaiah Thomas (basketball)|Isaiah Thomas]], [[Jae Crowder]], [[Ante Žižić]] and the [[Brooklyn Nets]] first round draft pick, later used for Alabama star Collin Sexton. Towards the beginning of the season there was rumors of LeBron possibly leaving Cleveland again in free agency. The Cavaliers finished with a record of 50–32 and earned the 4th seed. Meanwhile, for Chicago they finished with {{win-loss record|w=27|l=55}}. The Cavaliers beat the fifth seeded [[2017–18 Indiana Pacers season|Pacers]], first seeded [[2017–18 Toronto Raptors season|Raptors]], and second seeded [[2017–18 Boston Celtics season|Celtics]] to make their fourth straight finals appearance. However they would fall to [[2017–18 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State]] led by [[Kevin Durant]] and Stephen Curry again, this time getting swept. The [[2018 NBA draft]] came with possible big NBA stars, and Chicago took [[Wendell Carter Jr.]] with their 7th pick, and Cleveland took [[Collin Sexton]] straight afterwards with the 8th pick. The LeBron rumors for Cleveland would turn out to be true, as he signed a 4-year $154 million deal with the Lakers. Both Cleveland and Chicago entered the rebuilding stages, with Cleveland returning the playoffs beginning [[2023 NBA playoffs|2023]] and the Bulls making the [[2022 NBA playoffs|2022 playoffs]].

On January 2, 2023, the Cavaliers' [[Donovan Mitchell]] scored 71 points against the Bulls for the highest scoring performance since [[Kobe Bryant|Kobe Bryant's 81-point game]] in 2006 and leading the Cavaliers past a 21-point deficit to an overtime win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/game/chi-vs-cle-0022200552|title=Chicago Bulls vs. Cleveland Cavaliers Jan 2, 2023 Game Summary|website=NBA.com|accessdate=August 13, 2026}}</ref> 

The Cavaliers and Bulls faced-off under East Group C in the [[2024 NBA Cup]], with the Cavaliers winning the group stage game on November 15 with a score of 144–126.<ref name=nbacup2024>{{cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/news/emirates-nba-cup-2024-group-play-schedule|title=Group Play schedule unveiled for Emirates NBA Cup 2024|accessdate=August 18, 2024|website=NBA.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022400013|title=Chicago Bulls vs Cleveland Cavaliers Nov 15, 2024 Game Summary|accessdate=November 29, 2024|website=NBA.com}}</ref> With both teams eventually finishing the group stage with a 2–2 record, this game secured the head-to-head tiebreaker for the Cavaliers to place 3rd and the Bulls 4th in such group, which was won by the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. 

On July 6, 2025, during the offseason, the Bulls and Cavaliers agreed to a trade that sent [[Lonzo Ball]] to the Cavaliers in exchange for [[Isaac Okoro]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bulls acquire Isaac Okoro from Cleveland Cavaliers {{!}} Chicago Bulls |url=https://bulls.com/news/chicago-bulls-acquire-isaac-okoro-from-cleveland-cavaliers |access-date=2025-07-06 |website=bulls.com |language=en}}</ref>
